This neuron is essentially a detector of the sub-word prefix "uns"/"Uns"/"UNS" (as in *unsaturated, unsightly, unsung*), which drives it strongly negative, while its weak positive end fires on ordinary continuation/word-piece tokens, notably the fragment immediately following a separate "un-" prefix ("un|gl|ued", "un|tr|oub|led") and common function words like " been"/" there".

L11·N2972unmasked layer
Weak, low-selectivity neuron that peaks on ordinary mid-sentence tokens opening a new predicate or noun phrase (a verb right after a pronoun subject, the article "a", the first piece of a proper name/noun like "D"-ali or "child"), while being strongly suppressed on the completing token of fixed idiomatic collocations ("take **advantage** of", "making the **most** of", "life-aff**irm**ing", "fl**ing**").
